transcript.text: micrwave keeps tripping the eletric, not every time but like 1 in 3 when i press start, whole kitchen goes off. had to reset the fuse box 4 times today

Stop using the microwave and unplug it if you can do so safely. Repeated tripping—especially several times in one day—can indicate an electrical fault in the microwave, its plug/lead, or the kitchen circuit. Don’t keep resetting the fuse box and trying again.

What to do:

• Leave the microwave unplugged and don’t use it until it has been checked, repaired, or replaced.
• Check for obvious damage to the plug, cable, socket, scorch marks, burning smell, buzzing, or moisture. If any are present, do not touch/use it and arrange an electrician urgently.
• If the kitchen circuit now stays on with the microwave unplugged, the microwave is very likely the issue. Have it professionally repaired/tested or replace it—microwaves contain high-voltage parts and should not be opened DIY.
• If the circuit trips with the microwave unplugged, or trips when other appliances are used, contact a qualified electrician (or your landlord/agent if renting) promptly; there may be a wiring/socket/circuit fault.
• If there is smoke, heat, burning smell, sparking, or the breaker will not stay on, switch off the relevant circuit/main supply if safe and seek urgent electrical help.

A trip only “1 in 3 times” still isn’t normal; it can happen when an internal fault appears only once the microwave’s high-voltage components start up.
